claim.pdf_says: 14.9.19.4  General rules  — a fourth-level clause heading under 14.9.19 IF statement, identical in rank to 14.9.19.1/.2/.3.
claim.markdown_says: ## 14.9.19.4 General rules   (specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 27501 — level 2, while '### 14.9.19.1 General', '### 14.9.19.2 General formats' and '### 14.9.19.3 Syntax rules' are level 3)
claim.why_it_matters: Same promotion defect: General rules for the IF statement renders as a sibling of the IF statement clause instead of a child, corrupting the heading tree.

verdict.reasoning: Confirmed by rendering both the target page and its predecessor at 300 dpi and reading the printed glyphs directly. PDF page 666 (printed folio 636) carries exactly one heading: bold serif '14.9.19.4   General rules', set at the same left margin (x-height and weight indistinguishable) as the headings on PDF page 665 (folio 635), which prints '14.9.19 IF statement', '14.9.19.1  General', '14.9.19.2  General formats' and '14.9.19.3  Syntax rules'. Typographically .4 is the identical rank to .1/.2/.3 and one rank below the parent 14.9.19 — so the PDF side of the claim is quoted accurately. The markdown side is also accurate as to substance: grep of specs/ISO_COBOL.md returns '## 14.9.19 IF statement' (27456), '### 14.9.19.1 General' (27459), '### 14.9.19.2 General formats' (27464), '### 14.9.19.3 Syntax rules' (27477), then '## 14.9.19.4 General rules' — level 2. The .4 heading is therefore emitted as a SIBLING of its own parent clause and as a NON-sibling of its three numeric peers, which is both wrong against the PDF and internally self-contradictory within the transcription. I attempted to refute this as formatting furniture and could not: no page-break artifact, reflow, hyphenation or wrapping is involved, the heading sits mid-page well clear of the page boundary, and the defect is a hash-count difference that a markdown heading-tree consumer (TOC generation, section-scoped citation lookup, ancestor resolution for '14.9.19.4' -> '14.9.19' -> '14.9' -> '14') resolves incorrectly. Body text is fully intact and verbatim: FORMAT 2 rule 3), the '14.9.19.4 General rules' title itself, FORMAT 1 rules 1)-2) and FORMAT 2 rules 3)-7) all transcribe faithfully with no dropped or altered normative wording, so this is a tree defect only, not a content-loss defect. Two inaccuracies in how the claim was written, neither of which defeats it, are corrected below.
verdict.corrected_description: REAL, but mislabeled and off-by-three on the line number. (1) kind should be 'heading-level' / 'heading-promotion', NOT 'missing-heading' — nothing is missing; the heading text '14.9.19.4 General rules' is present and character-for-character correct. The sole defect is that it is emitted at markdown level 2 (##) instead of level 3 (###). (2) The cited line 27501 is wrong: line 27503 holds the anchor '' and line 27504 holds '## 14.9.19.4 General rules'. (3) Most important for remediation: this is NOT an isolated instance and must not be fixed as a one-line edit. specs/ISO_COBOL.md contains 162 four-digit headings emitted at level 2 against 620 emitted correctly at level 3 — a systematic ~21% transcription defect spanning the document (e.g. '## 6.2.3.2 Syntax rules' line 2947, '## 7.2.4.4 General rules' line 3587, and the immediate neighbours of this instance: '## 14.9.18.4 General rules' line 27392 for GOBACK and '## 14.9.20.4 General rules' line 27603 for INITIALIZE, whose own .1/.2/.3 siblings are all level 3). The correct remediation is a mechanical sweep demoting every '^## N.N.N.N ' heading to '### ', not a per-page patch. Severity 'structural' is appropriate: no normative text is lost, but the derived heading tree is corrupted for 162 clauses.
